evidence.note: First run_tests invocation; agent reads aggregate result 68170/68186 and immediately characterizes the 16 failures by method type ('mostly no-position methods and a couple position methods'), showing it tracks not just the aggregate but which method categories are failing.

Agent drills into the failing subset, rules out duplicate-key collisions, and localizes root cause to URI path stripping (/workspace/test-files vs /workspace/java). This is targeted failure localization tied to the pass/fail count rather than blind churning.

After the fix, agent confirms count moved to 68186/68186 reward 1.0 and stops. Whole horizon was only two test runs — no regressions occurred and no repeated circling on a single failure, so higher-anchor behaviors (live ledger, thrash detection, prioritizing by expected gain) were never exercised.

reasoning: The agent tracked the aggregate pass count and broke failures down by method category, then localized the exact cause of the 16 failing cases — matching the level-5 anchor (tracks which methods pass vs fail, notices the count and acts on it). It does not reach level 8: because the golden-cache approach passed nearly everything at once, there was no long-horizon per-method ledger, no regressions to catch, and no episode of circular debugging to step back from. The short two-run trajectory simply never demanded, nor demonstrated, sustained progress discipline beyond the aggregate-plus-failure-category view.
